Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe. The interior of the turbine was illuminated using an external light source. The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed for documentation and comparison during future inspections. It is important to note that due to the magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified. It is also important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by lens distortion. As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a photograph. This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual condition of the area. However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination. Interpretation of the photographs should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. Access to the turbine section was possible through the BI ports for each stage located on the top of the unit. Additional access to S1N and S1B was possible through the DLN on can 12. GE Power Inspection & Life Extension Services Observations Peripherals Not inspected. The plugs not being able to be removed Compressor Section All the compressor show evidence of deposits and oxidation/corrosion in stage 8 to 14. The R4 blades that were examined show tip curl. The R5 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a one blade. The R8 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a couple of blades. The R9 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a one blade. The R12 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a one blade. The R13 blades that were examined show lower case rub and tip curl. The R14 blades that were examined show lower case rub. The S14 vanes that were examined show tip curl on the vanes at the six o’clock position. Rotor rub was also observed. Stages 15-17 blades and vanes were not inspected due to all 6 CDC plugs not being able to be removed. Combustion Section All 14 effusion plates show deposits and oxidation/erosion. The effusion plates in cans 1, 5, 8 each show 1 crack. Cans 6, 11, 13 and 14 each show 2 cracks. The PM3 in can 11 show evidence of what appear to be burning/erosion. Turbine Section The S1N that were examined show Pressure Side chordal cracks on numerous vanes. Inner Sidewall oxidation/erosion was observed at several segment joints. Additionally, Outer Sidewall relief radius cracks were observed. Inner Sidewall and Outer Sidewall TBC spallation and cracks were also observed. GE Power Inspection & Life Extension Services The S1B that were examined show LE Suction Side TBC spallation. Rub was also observed on the LE of the blade platforms. Additionally, TBC spallation and wear was observed on the blade tips. The S1S that was examined show TBC spallation as well as oxidation/erosion. The S2N that were examined show LE PS chordal cracks. TE cracks were also observed. Additionally, Inner Sidewall relief radius cracks were observed. The S2B that were examined show oxidation/erosion on the outer side of the blade shroud tips. The S2S honeycomb that was examined show in good condition. The S3N that were examined show LE Pressure Side deposits. The S3B that were examined show LE blend repairs. The S3S honeycomb that was examined show in good condition
